mutants.desc: the compact settings arm no longer checks the handle's health itself
mutants.cmd: test --locked --offline --lib -- compact::source::seam_tests

equivalent.argument: set_collection_settings calls resolve first and resolve begins with ensure_healthy, so the call in the compact arm repeats a check that has just passed. Nothing between the two calls can change the flag a test can set. Only the flusher thread failing inside that window could, and the arm's check cannot close it either, because the same window reopens before commit_frame. The invariant is kept by resolve and pinned at the behavior level.
equivalent.invariant: a poisoned handle answers Poisoned before validation, before the read-only gate and before any scan of the base
equivalent.addendum: Added on 2026-11-05 when the evidence was replayed on the integration tree int072-c1 (after the review below, whose text stands unchanged). On that tree the compact arm sits in set_live_collection_settings, which has two callers: set_collection_settings (after resolve) and the server layer's set_settings_by_id in src/by_id.rs (after live_collection). resolve and live_collection both begin with ensure_healthy, so the argument holds for both callers. The pin test drives set_collection_settings only; a pin for the by-id caller would be a new test, which the frozen tree does not carry.
equivalent.caveat: Flusher::failed() is an atomic that the background flusher can set, and ensure_healthy reads it together with the poisoned flag. The call in resolve and the call in the compact arm of set_collection_settings therefore differ only if the flusher fails in the few instructions between them: the second call would then answer Poisoned instead of continuing to a later error (the validation) or to the commit. No contract orders that case and no deterministic test can observe it. The call stays in the code.
equivalent.review: accepted by the coordinator, 2026-11-05 PT. Checked on b8a1e67c: set_collection_settings takes &mut self and calls self.resolve(name)? first (lib.rs 2913); resolve begins with self.ensure_healthy()? (lib.rs 2727-2728); the compact arm's own self.ensure_healthy()? (lib.rs 2916) re-reads the same poisoned flag and the Flusher::failed() atomic, so no deterministic schedule can tell the two apart. The pin test and the pin mutant x-health-gate-inert show that the unhealthy-database error is pinned through resolve.
